# Government screening is expanding the diagnosed pool

The Government of India announced the "75/25" initiative in May 2023: put **75
million people living with hypertension and diabetes on standardised care by
December 2025**, described at launch as the largest primary-care
non-communicable-disease coverage programme in the world.

As of 5 March 2025, **42.01 million individuals had been treated for
hypertension** and 25.27 million for diabetes, reaching roughly 89.7 per cent of
the combined target. A national NCD screening campaign ran from 20 February to
31 March 2025 aiming at 100 per cent screening of adults aged 30 and above,
delivered through Ayushman Arogya Mandir facilities under the NP-NCD framework.

## Why this matters for prioritisation

Screening programmes convert undiagnosed prevalence into diagnosed, treated
patients. The first-line therapies that benefit are the ones on public
formularies and standard treatment protocols - single-molecule
anti-hypertensives and plain statins - rather than premium combinations.

This is a genuine volume tailwind, but it is a **mixed signal for value**:
public-channel volume typically carries lower realised price than private
retail. It supports the volume-growth reading in the scoring engine while
arguing against over-weighting reported value growth in the same spaces.
